title: GPS Spoofing WorkGroup 2024 - Final Report
summary: Crowd-sourced industry report from a six-week OPSGROUP workgroup of pilots, controllers, regulators and manufacturers on GPS spoofing hitting civil flights, mainly near Middle East and Black Sea / Baltic conflict areas. Comes with crew guidance and a technical guide.
key_takeaways: Spoofing degrades terrain-warning (EGPWS) functions, which may stay wrong after GPS returns
No quick fix: mitigation is crew awareness, procedures and keeping ground navaids
Strong evidence that integrity monitoring and 'is my position plausible?' checks matter more than raw accuracy

title: EASA SIB 2022-02R3: Global Navigation Satellite System Outage and Alterations Leading to Communication / Navigation / Surveillance Degradation
summary: EASA's safety information bulletin on GNSS jamming and spoofing affecting aircraft, revised repeatedly since 2022 as interference spread around conflict zones. Lists symptoms and recommendations for authorities, ANSPs, operators and manufacturers; later revisions (R4) followed.
key_takeaways: Spoofing is harder for crews to detect than jamming and so the bigger safety risk
Recommends cross-checking with non-GNSS navaids and reporting events
Affected flight information regions are tracked on EASA's GNSS page

title: EASA - Global Navigation Satellite System outages and alterations
summary: EASA's landing page for GNSS interference: current SIB revision, affected regions and related guidance and workshops.
key_takeaways: Single place to check the current bulletin revision
Links civil-aviation guidance to the interference geography

title: EASA and IATA comprehensive plan to mitigate the risks of GNSS interference
summary: Joint plan from a May 2025 EASA/IATA workshop setting out actions on reporting and monitoring, prevention and mitigation, airspace/infrastructure (backup navaids) and civil-military coordination against GNSS interference.
key_takeaways: Four pillars: reporting, prevention, infrastructure, coordination
Retaining conventional navaids is explicitly part of resilience
Calls for better civil-military sharing of interference data

title: FAA SAFO 24002: Recognizing and Mitigating GPS/GNSS Disruptions
summary: FAA Safety Alert for Operators describing jamming vs spoofing effects on aircraft systems, typical locations near conflict and counter-UAS areas, and recommended crew and operator actions.
key_takeaways: Hybrid GPS/inertial solutions can also be corrupted by spoofing
Revert to conventional procedures and report to ATC
Disruptions cluster around conflict zones and C-UAS protection areas

title: SKYbrary - GNSS Jamming and Spoofing
summary: Aviation-safety wiki article explaining jamming and spoofing, observed effects on aircraft avionics and links to regulator guidance.
key_takeaways: Good primer on how interference propagates through avionics
Collects links to EASA, FAA and ICAO material

title: Above Us Only Stars: Exposing GPS Spoofing in Russia and Syria
summary: Open-source investigation using AIS ship tracks, public records and ISS-based measurements to map thousands of GNSS spoofing events around Russia, Crimea and Syria, many linked to protection of VIPs and bases.
key_takeaways: Shows how public data (AIS) reveals spoofing via impossible tracks
Spoofing used for airspace denial around military facilities
A model for OSINT-style interference detection projects

title: GPSJam - daily GPS interference map
summary: Daily world map of likely GPS interference derived from ADS-B navigation-integrity reports (NIC/NACp) aggregated into hexagons from community flight-tracking data. The FAQ documents the method and its blind spots.
key_takeaways: Interference is inferred from aircraft self-reported integrity, not measured RF
Empty cells mean no data, not no jamming
Easy to reproduce with your own ADS-B receiver

title: Bellingcat OSINT Toolkit - GPSJam
summary: Bellingcat's toolkit entry on using GPSJam for open-source investigations, with notes on limitations and interpretation.
key_takeaways: Frames interference maps as OSINT evidence with caveats
Useful for teams building verification workflows

title: ADS-B Data Analysis for GNSS Interference Mapping
summary: Trade-press article on using ADS-B integrity data to detect and map GNSS interference regions.
key_takeaways: ADS-B is an existing, free sensor network for interference awareness
Method details help design your own detector

title: GNSS interference report: Russia 2024/2025 - Part 1: Kaliningrad and the Baltic Sea
summary: Spire analysis using satellite-received ADS-B integrity metrics and RF data to characterize persistent interference around Kaliningrad and over the Baltic.
key_takeaways: Satellite ADS-B extends interference monitoring over sea areas
Kaliningrad is a persistent Baltic interference zone

title: Researchers home in on origins of Russia's Baltic GPS jamming
summary: Reporting on Gdynia Maritime University and DLR work combining ground monitoring stations with aviation data to localize Baltic jamming emitters.
key_takeaways: Emitter localization from distributed monitors plus ADS-B is feasible
Baltic interference has shifted to include spoofing

title: Spoofing now affecting commercial flights
summary: Post from Todd Humphreys' lab on spoofing incidents hitting commercial aircraft and what they show about receiver and avionics vulnerability.
key_takeaways: Academic view on why civil receivers accept spoofed signals
Points toward authentication and cross-checks as defenses

title: GPS Spoofing in the Civil Aviation Sector (RIN 2024)
summary: Royal Institute of Navigation event microsite gathering expert talks on spoofing affecting airlines and possible mitigations.
key_takeaways: UK navigation-community perspective
Covers detection, operations and policy angles

title: Windward - 2025 maritime stress test
summary: Maritime-intelligence review of 2025 including large-scale GNSS jamming and spoofing in the Gulf and Strait of Hormuz after the June 2025 Israel-Iran strikes.
key_takeaways: Hundreds of ships per day affected at the peak
AIS anomalies are the main public signal of GNSS manipulation at sea

title: Meatgrinder: Russian Tactics in the Second Year of Its Invasion of Ukraine
summary: RUSI special report on Russian battlefield adaptation, including the density of Russian electronic warfare and its heavy effect on Ukrainian UAVs, with a widely cited estimate of around 10,000 drone losses per month.
key_takeaways: Dense EW coverage along the front is weighted toward defeating UAVs
Loss figures came from interviews and are contested
Explains why EW-resilient navigation became a top Ukrainian requirement

title: Space Threat Assessment 2025
summary: Annual CSIS Aerospace Security Project review of counterspace capabilities, with sections on GPS jamming and spoofing in Eastern Europe and the Middle East.
key_takeaways: Puts terrestrial GNSS jamming in the wider counterspace picture
Useful citation for problem framing in pitches

title: The invisible war: Inside the electronic warfare arms race that could shape course of the war
summary: Long-form reporting on the EW and counter-EW cycle in Ukraine, covering jamming of drones and navigation and the rapid iteration of countermeasures.
key_takeaways: Adaptation cycles are measured in weeks
Frequency agility and non-GNSS navigation are recurring answers

title: Ukrainian military's anti-drone GPS spoofing spills into civilians' phones
summary: Report on Ukraine's nationwide defensive spoofing against incoming drones and missiles, and its side effects on civilian devices' location and time.
key_takeaways: Defensive spoofing has collateral effects on civil PNT and timing
Any consumer-grade nav stack must tolerate wrong GNSS

title: Ukrainian drones use Vermeer optical navigation system
summary: Ukrainian defense outlet report on a visual positioning system integrated on drones used by Ukrainian forces for operation when GNSS is jammed.
key_takeaways: Vision-based absolute positioning against reference imagery is being fielded
Vendor claims are not independently tested

title: NATO DIANA unveils 10 new challenges to accelerate dual-use technology breakthroughs
summary: Announcement of DIANA's 2026 challenge programme topics, including operating in contested electromagnetic environments, with problem statements that describe what NATO wants solved.
key_takeaways: Problem statements stress dual-use and resilience in contested spectrum
Good template for writing a hackathon pitch in NATO language

title: NATO DIANA's breakthrough solutions for secure communication and navigation
summary: DIANA feature on cohort companies working on resilient navigation and secure communications, illustrating which approaches made it through selection.
key_takeaways: Shows the spread of selected approaches: magnetic, quantum, LEO PNT, vision
Selection favors deployable, testable dual-use products

title: Ukraine's Brave1, NATO launch EUR 10M competition for counter-drone technology
summary: Coverage of a Brave1-NATO competition funding counter-drone technology and navigation that works under electronic warfare.
key_takeaways: Brave1 frames navigation under EW as a top battlefield need
Competitions emphasize rapid field testing

title: В Україні провели хакатон зі створення антидронових рішень (Anti-drone hackathon held in Ukraine)
summary: Ukrainian-language report on a defense hackathon focused on counter-drone solutions.
key_takeaways: Ukrainian hackathons are short, problem-driven and tied to frontline users
Detection and EW-resilience recur as tracks

title: DIU solicitation: Transition of Quantum Sensing for navigation
summary: Coverage of DIU's Transition of Quantum Sensing call seeking quantum inertial sensors and magnetometers to extend navigation holdover when GPS is unavailable.
key_takeaways: DIU's stated value: reduced drift means longer holdover without GPS
Lines of effort: inertial, magnetometers, technology insertion
Magnetic anomaly navigation is a funded transition path

title: DARPA eying new quantum sensing program: Robust Quantum Sensors (RoQS)
summary: Report on DARPA's RoQS program to make quantum sensors robust to platform interference so they can support navigation without GPS on real vehicles.
key_takeaways: Platform noise, not lab sensitivity, is the barrier DARPA targets
Context for why classical magnetic compensation still matters

title: DARPA PNT programs briefing to the National Space-Based PNT Advisory Board (2019)
summary: DARPA slide deck summarizing its PNT portfolio, including All Source Positioning and Navigation (ASPN), a plug-and-play architecture for fusing non-traditional sensors when GPS is denied.
key_takeaways: ASPN pushes sensor-agnostic, plug-and-play fusion
Shows the long-running DoD interest in all-source navigation

title: EDF-2024-LS-RA-CHALLENGE-SENS-RADNP: Multi-sensor integration for robust autonomous drone navigation
summary: European Defence Fund technological-challenge topic on multi-sensor integration for autonomous drone navigation in GNSS-denied or contested environments, run as an organized competition with evaluation campaigns. Listing via an aggregator; confirm details on the EU Funding and Tenders portal.
key_takeaways: EU frames GNSS-denied drone navigation as a benchmarked challenge
Multi-sensor fusion, not a single sensor, is the ask

title: EDF 2021 NAVGUARD project factsheet
summary: Factsheet for an EDF-funded project developing ground and space-based detection of illegitimate activity in GNSS bands.
key_takeaways: Interference detection and monitoring is a funded European priority
Pairs well with ADS-B/SDR monitoring hackathon ideas

title: DASA competition: Advanced Radio Frequency Sensing, Integrated Effects and PNT
summary: UK DASA themed competition (for the Bright Corvus project) seeking RF sensing and resilient PNT innovations.
key_takeaways: UK MOD treats RF sensing and PNT as one problem space
Example of UK-style challenge framing

title: Positioning, navigation and timing growth: government response
summary: UK government response on growing the resilient PNT sector, following its national PNT framework work.
key_takeaways: UK policy treats resilient PNT as both security and export opportunity
Useful framing for dual-use pitches

title: Resilient PNT Conformance Framework
summary: Outcome-based framework defining four levels of resilience for PNT equipment (from recovery to full threat tolerance), developed under Executive Order 13905.
key_takeaways: Gives vocabulary to grade your solution: prevent, respond, recover
Solution-agnostic, so it fits any sensor mix
Later versions and an IEEE standards effort followed

title: NISTIR 8323: Foundational PNT Profile - Applying the Cybersecurity Framework for the Responsible Use of PNT Services
summary: Maps the NIST Cybersecurity Framework onto systems that consume PNT, giving identify/protect/detect/respond/recover practices for GNSS dependence.
key_takeaways: Treats GNSS as an untrusted external input
Detection and recovery practices map directly to hackathon features

title: HACKtheMACHINE Unmanned (ONR / NavalX)
summary: US Navy prize challenge on unmanned and autonomous systems with tracks on securing a simulated autopilot, separating benign from malicious data, and model-based mission requirements.
key_takeaways: Navy judges reward working prototypes on realistic simulated systems
Cyber-resilience of autopilots is treated as part of autonomy

title: Space Security Challenge 2022: Hack-A-Sat 3
summary: AFRL/Space Force capture-the-flag on satellite and ground-segment security; challenge code from several editions has been released publicly.
key_takeaways: Space-segment security is part of assured PNT
Released challenges are good training material

title: DARPA Subterranean (SubT) Challenge
summary: DARPA's 2018-2021 challenge for autonomous robot teams mapping and searching tunnels, urban underground and caves with no GNSS and degraded comms; systems and virtual tracks.
key_takeaways: Scoring rewarded accurate localization of reported artifacts, not just coverage
Heterogeneous teams (legged + aerial) won
Communication-denied autonomy was decisive

title: DARPA Triage Challenge
summary: DARPA challenge for autonomous systems that find and assess casualties in mass-casualty scenes, combining drones and ground robots navigating degraded, GNSS-unreliable environments.
key_takeaways: Humanitarian defense use-case with navigation plus perception
Team directory helps find open contributions

title: A Multi-Robot Platform for Robotic Triage
summary: Technical report from a DARPA Triage Challenge team describing a multi-robot system and fine-tuned open vision-language models for injury identification.
key_takeaways: Shows how a challenge team integrates navigation, perception and VLMs
Open-model fine-tuning is viable under challenge time budgets

title: Signal Enhancement for Magnetic Navigation Challenge Problem
summary: Defines the AFRL/MIT MagNav challenge: remove the aircraft's own magnetic field from airborne magnetometer data so the Earth's anomaly field can be used for navigation, with released flight data and a scientific-ML baseline.
key_takeaways: Problem is compensation, the hard step before map matching
Physics (Tolles-Lawson) plus ML beat either alone
Data and baseline code are open

title: MagNav challenge flight data (Sander Geophysics, Zenodo)
summary: Zenodo record of airborne magnetometer, INS and GNSS flight data with datasheets, collected for the MagNav challenge.
key_takeaways: Real flight lines with multiple magnetometers
Ground truth from GNSS for evaluating nav error

title: Team CERBERUS Wins the DARPA Subterranean Challenge: Technical Overview and Lessons Learned
authors: Team CERBERUS (NTNU, ETH Zurich, UNR, Oxford, et al.)
summary: Winning team's description of its legged-plus-aerial system: multi-modal perception, robust localization and mapping, exploration planning and artifact detection, with lessons from the final.
key_takeaways: Robust multi-sensor odometry and exploration were key
Field-hardening and operator workflow mattered as much as algorithms

title: CERBERUS: Autonomous Legged and Aerial Robotic Exploration in the Tunnel and Urban Circuits of the DARPA Subterranean Challenge
summary: Field Robotics paper covering CERBERUS' systems and results in the earlier SubT circuits, including perception, planning and artifact reporting.
key_takeaways: Documents the iteration path to the winning system

title: NeBula: Quest for Robotic Autonomy in Challenging Environments; TEAM CoSTAR at the DARPA Subterranean Challenge
summary: Describes the NeBula belief-space autonomy stack: multi-modal positioning, mapping, traversability, risk-aware mission planning and multi-robot reasoning; CoSTAR won the Urban circuit.
key_takeaways: Reasoning over uncertainty in localization improves mission decisions
Redundant odometry sources were essential underground

title: AlphaPilot: Autonomous Drone Racing
summary: UZH's second-place AlphaPilot system: learned gate detection, nonlinear filtering of visual-inertial state and time-optimal trajectory planning for GPS-free racing.
key_takeaways: Vision-inertial state estimation, not GNSS, drove the race
Splitting perception and planning made it robust

title: MAVLab wins the AlphaPilot challenge
summary: TU Delft MAVLab's account of winning the 2019 Lockheed Martin AlphaPilot / AIRR autonomous drone race.
key_takeaways: Lightweight onboard estimation can beat heavier stacks
Same lab later won A2RL 2025

title: Champion-level drone racing using deep reinforcement learning
summary: Swift, a quadrotor using only onboard camera and IMU with an RL-trained policy, beat human world-champion pilots in head-to-head races.
key_takeaways: Onboard VIO plus learned control reached human-champion level
Sim-to-real with residual models from real data

title: 2025 Abu Dhabi Autonomous Racing League (A2RL) - drone championship
summary: Summary of the A2RL x DCL autonomous drone championship, won by TU Delft MAVLab ahead of TII Racing and KAIST, including races against human pilots.
key_takeaways: Standardized drone and camera-only sensing put the focus on estimation and control
University labs still beat well-funded teams

title: Satellite Pose Estimation Challenge: Dataset, Competition Design and Results
summary: ESA Kelvins / Stanford competition on monocular spacecraft pose estimation, analyzing 48 entries.
key_takeaways: Keypoint detection plus PnP beat direct pose regression
Shows how ESA designs and scores a navigation competition

title: ESA Kelvins Satellite Pose Estimation Competition 2021 (SPEED+)
summary: Follow-up Kelvins challenge focused on bridging the domain gap: train on synthetic images, test on hardware-in-the-loop lightbox and sunlamp images.
key_takeaways: Sim-to-real gap is the core difficulty judges scored
Kelvins pages document rules and metrics

title: Stone Soup documentation and tutorials
summary: Official docs for Dstl's tracking framework with tutorials on Kalman, particle and multi-target trackers, data association and metrics.
key_takeaways: Tutorial path from single-target Kalman to multi-target
Metrics module helps score your fusion objectively

title: Drone Security and the Mysterious Case of DJI's DroneID
summary: Reverse-engineers DJI's DroneID broadcast, shows it is unencrypted, and builds an SDR receiver that decodes drone and pilot positions.
key_takeaways: Passive decoding enables detection and localization of DJI drones
Security analysis of drone firmware and protocols

title: FAA - Remote Identification of Drones
summary: FAA guidance on the Remote ID rule: what drones must broadcast, standard vs broadcast-module compliance and operator obligations.
key_takeaways: Remote ID gives a lawful, cooperative signal for drone awareness
Defines what fields you can expect to decode

title: The EAR and Open Source Software
summary: Practical guide to how US Export Administration Regulations treat published open-source code, including the separate notification step for encryption.
key_takeaways: Code published without restriction is generally outside the EAR
Encryption source has an extra BIS/NSA notification step
Private repos shared with foreign nationals can count as exports

title: 15 CFR 734.7 - Published (Export Administration Regulations)
authors: US Bureau of Industry and Security
summary: The regulation text defining when information and software count as 'published' and therefore not subject to the EAR.
key_takeaways: Primary source to cite in an export-control slide
Read with 734.3(b)(3) and 742.15(b)

title: U.S. Export Controls and Published Encryption Source Code Explained
summary: EFF explainer on the 2016-era EAR changes for published encryption source and when email notification is still needed.
key_takeaways: Relevant if your PNT code includes signal authentication crypto

title: Regulatory Definitions of Publicly Available, Public Domain, and Published (ITAR/EAR)
summary: University compliance guide comparing ITAR public-domain (22 CFR 120.34) and EAR published definitions and the fundamental-research exclusion.
key_takeaways: ITAR-controlled data cannot simply be put in the public domain by an individual
Fundamental-research protection can be lost via publication restrictions
Military GNSS items (e.g. M-code receivers, some anti-jam antenna tech) may be ITAR or EAR controlled - keep hackathon code on public civil signals and published methods

title: DOD adopts 5 principles of artificial intelligence ethics
summary: Announcement of the DoD's AI ethical principles - responsible, equitable, traceable, reliable, governable - recommended by the Defense Innovation Board.
key_takeaways: Traceable and governable map to logging and safe fallback in nav autonomy
Judges increasingly ask how an AI component can be disengaged

title: Summary of the NATO Artificial Intelligence Strategy (Principles of Responsible Use)
summary: NATO's 2021 AI strategy summary setting six principles of responsible use: lawfulness, responsibility and accountability, explainability and traceability, reliability, governability, bias mitigation.
key_takeaways: Applies across the whole AI lifecycle
Expect a NATO-flavored jury to probe reliability and governability

title: DoD Directive 3000.09: Autonomy in Weapon Systems (2023 reissue)
summary: DoD policy governing development and use of autonomous and semi-autonomous weapon systems, reissued January 2023. Cited here as the boundary marker: navigation and awareness tools are outside its scope, weapon autonomy is not.
key_takeaways: Clear line between navigation/autonomy for mobility and weapon autonomy
Keep hackathon scope on the navigation and awareness side

title: Regulation (EU) 2021/821 - Dual-use export control regime
summary: The EU's recast dual-use export control regulation covering items, software and technology including navigation and avionics categories, with public-domain and basic-research de-control notes.
key_takeaways: Category 7 covers navigation and avionics items
Public-domain and basic scientific research notes protect open publication

title: Commission Recommendation (EU) 2021/1700 on internal compliance programmes for controls of research involving dual-use items
summary: Non-binding guidance helping universities and researchers spot and manage dual-use export risks, with scenarios, red flags and FAQs.
key_takeaways: Practical red-flag checklist for collaborative or international teams
Contact national authority when control status is unclear
